# tfcensus notify

notify reads the JSON that scan, drift and audit print with --format json and publishes it.
It never collects anything itself.

```text
slack                 one message per report to an incoming webhook, with counts and the top
                      findings; sent only when there is something to report (notify.slack.when)
github-issues         one issue per scope: per unit for drift, per account for scan and audit.
                      A re-run updates the body only when it changed, and closes the issue when
                      the run covered the scope and found nothing. notify.github_issues.max_open
                      caps new issues
github-pr-comment     one comment per report on a GitHub pull request, edited in place. The
                      pull request comes from GITHUB_EVENT_PATH; a report with nothing open
                      turns the comment into "Nothing to report"
bitbucket-pr-comment  one comment per report on a Bitbucket Cloud pull request, edited in place
file                  tfcensus-<kind>.md and .json in notify.file.dir, rewritten only on change
```

Every issue body and comment starts with a hidden marker that names the report kind, the scope
and a hash of the body, so runs find their own issues and skip unchanged ones. Only issues
with the tfcensus label are read.

Secrets come from the environment only: the variables named by notify.slack.webhook\_env,
notify.github\_issues.token\_env, notify.github\_pr\_comment.token\_env and
notify.bitbucket\_pr\_comment.token\_env. They are never
logged; -vvv shows request headers with Authorization redacted.

--dry-run-notify reads the existing issues and comments with GET requests and prints what
would change, writing nothing.

Exit codes: 0 when every notifier succeeded, 2 when no notifier is enabled, a notifier is
unknown or not configured, or a --from file is not a tfcensus report, 4 when every failure was a
refused token, and 1 for any other failure.

## Usage

```sh
tfcensus notify [flags]
```

## Flags

| Flag | Description | Type | Default | Values | Config key | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--dry-run-notify` | print what would change; read with GET only and write nothing | bool |  |  |  |  |
| `--from` | scan, drift or audit JSON file (repeatable) | string, repeatable |  |  |  |  |
| `--notify` | notifiers to run instead of notify.enabled: slack, github-issues, github-pr-comment, bitbucket-pr-comment or file | list, repeatable |  | `slack`: one message per report to an incoming webhook<br>`github-issues`: one GitHub issue per scope<br>`github-pr-comment`: one comment per report on a GitHub pull request<br>`bitbucket-pr-comment`: one comment per report on one pull request<br>`file`: tfcensus-&lt;kind&gt;.md and .json files |  |  |

The [global flags](/cli/global-flags) work with every command.

## Output formats

`--format` accepts `tty`, `plain`, `json`. Without it, the format is `tty` when stdout is a terminal and `plain` otherwise. Formats are described on the [global flags](/cli/global-flags) page.

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | The command finished. With --fail-on, nothing matched. |
| 1 | The command failed: a read, a write, a child process or a check failed. |
| 2 | Wrong usage: an unknown command or flag, a bad value or argument, an invalid config file, or a prompt with no terminal. |
| 4 | Credentials were missing or rejected for every source the command needed. |
| 130 | Interrupted by Ctrl-C (SIGINT) or a cancelled context. |

All codes are listed on the [exit codes](/reference/exit-codes) page.

## Examples

```sh
tfcensus drift --format json > drift.json; tfcensus notify --from drift.json --notify github-issues
tfcensus notify --from scan.json --from audit.json --dry-run-notify
tfcensus notify --from drift.json --notify github-pr-comment   # in a pull_request workflow
GITHUB_TOKEN=... tfcensus notify --from drift.json --notify github-issues,slack
```
